setup.title: Set up NurProxy
setup.intro: Two quick steps. New to this? <0>Read the guide</0>.
setup.tlsSub: NurProxy issues free HTTPS certificates for your domains automatically via Let's Encrypt (DNS-01). Let's Encrypt asks for a contact email.
setup.tlsPrivacyTitle: This email is only for Let's Encrypt
setup.tlsPrivacyBody: It is sent to the certificate authority (Let's Encrypt) so they can email you about expiring certificates and important account notices. It is NOT used to create a NurProxy account, is never sent to the NurProxy maintainers, and you will not receive any marketing from us.
setup.tlsEmailHelp: Leave blank to skip for now — you can add it later under Settings. Until it is set, automatic HTTPS certificates won't be issued.
setup.providerSub: Paste an API token and we’ll detect the domains it can manage.
setup.tokenHint: Needs <0>Zone → Read</0> and <1>DNS → Edit</1>. Stored encrypted at rest.
setup.whereBody: In Cloudflare, open <0>My Profile → API Tokens</0>, click <1>Create Token</1>, and use the <2>“Edit zone DNS”</2> template. You can scope it to only the zones you want, or all zones in your account. <3>Full walkthrough →</3>
setup.noZones: Token is valid, but no zones were found. Make sure it has Zone → Read for the domains you want.
setup.manageHint: You can manage domains under each zone afterwards.
setup.agentSub: Run the NurProxy agent on the edge server that will serve your traffic.
setup.orchestratorHint: This is how the agent reaches this dashboard. It must be reachable from the edge server — often a LAN IP, VPN address, or public hostname, not the URL in your browser’s address bar.
setup.fqdnHint: The public hostname for this edge server. The agent creates an A record for it at your DNS provider pointing to the server’s IP, and every subdomain you add for this agent becomes a CNAME to it. Change it only if you want a different anchor hostname than the server’s own FQDN.
setup.runThis: Run this on your edge server
setup.agentAdoptedBody: It’s connected and ready to serve domains.
setup.waiting: Waiting for the agent to connect…
setup.troubleReach: Make sure {{url}} is reachable from the edge server (try curl it there).
setup.troubleFirewall: Check the server’s firewall isn’t blocking outbound HTTPS.
setup.troubleLogs: Look at the agent logs for connection errors.
setup.noZonesYet: No zones yet — add a provider first.
setup.addLater: You can add more providers and agents anytime from Settings and Agents.

upgrade.title: Upgrade
upgrade.subtitle: Replace the agent binary with a new release. The agent downloads it, verifies it, restarts and rolls back on its own if it does not come back healthy.
upgrade.subtitleOutdated: This agent runs {{version}}, the orchestrator runs {{target}}. Upgrade it to keep both in step.
upgrade.unsupported: This agent cannot upgrade itself on its host.

disabled.in_progress: An upgrade is already running for this agent.

upgrade.dialogBody: The agent currently runs {{version}}. It downloads the new release, verifies it and restarts. If the new version does not report back healthy, the agent restores the previous one.
upgrade.versionHint: Leave empty to use the orchestrator's version ({{version}}).
upgrade.allowPrereleaseHint: Pre-releases (-rc, -beta) are refused unless you tick this.

state.requested: Upgrade to {{to}} requested, waiting for the agent
state.rolled_back: Upgrade to {{to}} rolled back, still on {{from}}

upgrade.autoHint: Off by default. When on, the agent is upgraded to the orchestrator's version whenever it falls behind. It never moves to any other version.
upgrade.historyFailed: Could not load the upgrade history.

rollout.noneOutdated: All agents are up to date.
rollout.confirmBody_other: {{count}} agents will be upgraded to {{version}}, one after another: {{names}}. Each agent has to come back healthy before the next one starts, and the rollout stops at the first failure so the remaining agents stay untouched.
rollout.confirmPrerelease: {{version}} is a pre-release. Starting the rollout installs it on these agents.
rollout.failed: Rollout to {{version}} stopped after a failure

agents.deleteConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? This removes all of its servers and domains too.
agents.anchorFqdnHelp: The DNS name that points at this server. It must live inside one of the agent’s zones — every domain you add becomes a CNAME to it.
agents.anchorFqdnWarn: This hostname isn’t inside any selected zone. DNS for it can’t be managed until you pick the matching zone or change the hostname.
agents.managingExistingShort: Manages the {{kind}} installed on this host.
agents.permFixHint: Run exactly these commands on the host (least-privilege, no blanket sudo):
agents.permWhyBody: NurProxy asks for the least it needs to manage your existing proxy: write its config directory, reload the service, and (as root) read its TLS keys. It never asks for blanket sudo or to run unconfined. Each command below grants exactly one of those, so you can see and audit what you give it. Run them on the host — the orchestrator never gets these rights itself.
agents.permExplainSandbox: The agent runs under a locked-down systemd unit that mounts the filesystem read-only and drops capabilities. This drop-in re-opens only the proxy's own config, log and runtime directories (ReadWritePaths) and, for a root agent, restores CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE so it can read the TLS keys and write the logs. Nothing else is loosened.
agents.permExplainSudoers: The agent runs as an unprivileged user, so reloading the proxy needs elevation. This grants a passwordless sudoers entry for exactly the test and reload commands, not blanket sudo. It lives in its own file under /etc/sudoers.d so it is easy to audit and remove.
agents.permExplainGroup: This makes the proxy's config directory group-writable and adds the agent's user to that group, so it can write config without sudo. The setgid bit makes new files inherit the group. No elevation, just file ownership.
agents.noProxyDetected: No supported reverse proxy detected on this host.
agents.bindConflictBody: Another process is holding the ports the built-in proxy needs. Switch this agent to an existing-proxy setup, or free the port.
agents.bindConflictChoiceFree: Stop the existing proxy and let the built-in proxy take the ports.
agents.bindConflictChoiceSwitch: Switch this agent to manage the existing proxy instead of running the built-in one —

recovery.title: Diagnosis & recovery
recovery.subtitle: Structured proxy faults, safe repairs, and durable operation history.
recovery.policySaveFailed: Could not save automatic repair policy.
recovery.upgradeRequiredBody: This agent has not advertised safe recovery support. Diagnosis remains visible, but repairs are disabled.
recovery.healthyBody: The agent has not reported any current or historical structured diagnostics.
recovery.helperBreakerBody: A managed apply on this agent failed and the helper could not prove a full rollback. It now refuses every further config change, so domains on this agent stay in error until the breaker is cleared.
recovery.leftoverVhostsTitle: Possibly leftover proxy config on this agent
recovery.leftoverVhostsBody: No route was sent for these NurProxy vhost files in the last apply, and no current domain on this agent matches them. The helper leaves them in place and keeps the certificates they reference. Check them before removing anything: a file may still hold config you want to keep.
recovery.helperBreakerClear: To clear it: on the agent host, fix the cause shown above until nginx -t (or apachectl configtest) passes and reload the proxy, move /var/lib/nurproxy-agent/helper/breaker.json out of the way, then restart nurproxy-agent-helper and nurproxy-agent. This message disappears after the next successful apply.
recovery.hardFirstConfirmed: First confirmation recorded. Review the unchanged plan once more.
recovery.hardExecutionAuthorized: Second confirmation recorded. Privileged execution is now authorized.
recovery.hardConfirmFailed: Privileged action could not be confirmed
recovery.freshPasswordLabel: Current admin password (required again for package and firewall changes)
recovery.helperEnrollmentBody: Run the root-only helper-bootstrap command on this agent host, then paste its signed public Hello envelope here. The private attestation key never leaves the host.
recovery.helperEnrollmentPlaceholder: Paste the signed helper Hello JSON
recovery.helperEnrollFailed: Recovery helper could not be enrolled
recovery.hardConfirmMessage: Review the complete privileged plan. Action: {{action}}. Bound target: {{target}}. Rollback coverage: {{coverage}}. Steps: {{steps}}. This first decision does not authorize execution yet.
recovery.hardFinalConfirmMessage: Confirm the same unchanged privileged plan a second time. Action: {{action}}. Bound target: {{target}}. Rollback coverage: {{coverage}}. Steps: {{steps}}. This decision issues a short-lived signed execution grant.
recovery.confirmMessage: NurProxy will execute the typed action “{{action}}” for: {{paths}}. No arbitrary command is sent.
recovery.confirmValidationMessage: The previous rollback failed. This explicit validation attempt will execute the typed action “{{action}}” for: {{paths}} and is the only way to clear the latch after a successful validation.
recovery.manualValidationEscape: Automatic repair stays blocked; this manual validation action remains available intentionally.

breakerReasons.failure_threshold: Three clustered repair failures paused further attempts.
breakerReasons.rollback_failed_latched: A failed rollback blocks automatic attempts until a successful manual validation.

resolutionReasons.resource_disappeared: the resource is no longer present
resolutionReasons.condition_no_longer_observed: the condition is no longer observed

reasons.hard_change: This system or privileged change is diagnosis-only in Stage 1.
reasons.ownership_not_nurproxy: NurProxy cannot prove ownership of this resource.
reasons.not_safe_repair_eligible: This diagnosis has no proven safe typed repair.
reasons.operation_active: A repair is already in progress.
reasons.recovery_capability_unavailable: Upgrade the agent to enable safe recovery.
reasons.action_unsupported: This agent does not support the proposed typed action.
reasons.circuit_breaker_open: The authoritative recovery circuit breaker is open.
reasons.hard_plan_pending: The connected helper has not published a current signed plan yet.
reasons.hard_plan_expired: This signed plan expired. Wait for a freshly discovered plan.
reasons.hard_execution_active: This plan is authorized or currently executing. Its receipt will appear automatically.
reasons.hard_execution_complete: The helper has already returned a signed receipt for this plan.
reasons.read_only_filesystem: The target filesystem is read-only; NurProxy will not try to bypass it.
reasons.selinux_or_apparmor_denied: SELinux or AppArmor denied access; no generic permission change is attempted.
reasons.immutable_or_append_only_target: The target is immutable or append-only; no automatic flag change is attempted.
reasons.unsupported_acl_semantics: The target uses unsupported ACL semantics; recovery remains diagnosis-only.
reasons.permission_scope_ambiguous: The safe permission scope cannot be proven, so no privileged mutation is offered.

existing.title: Set up Existing proxy
existing.intro: Manage a proxy already installed on this host instead of the built-in one. Confirm the detected paths below — you won’t usually need to change them.
existing.detectedBody: {{name}} was detected — the fields below are pre-filled from it. Confirm or adjust.
existing.noDetection: Nothing was detected for this proxy type. The fields are pre-filled with the OS defaults — confirm they match this host before applying.
existing.proxyKindHint: Which proxy this agent should manage. Pre-selected from detection.
existing.logPathsHint: One path per line. Surfaced in the dashboard for on-demand tailing.
existing.applyHint: Proxy mode lives in the agent’s own config. Add these keys to the agent’s config file (or pass them as flags) on the host, then restart the agent.
existing.permsNote: The agent must be able to write the config dir and run the reload/test commands — grant a group-owned dir plus a narrowly-scoped sudoers entry for exactly those commands, not blanket sudo.
existing.advancedHint: Prefer editing the file by hand? Add these keys to the agent’s config (agent.yaml) on the host, then restart the agent.
existing.runHint: Run one of these on the host where the agent lives. The agent claims the op with its local identity + this code, persists it, and hot-applies — no restart.
existing.dockerHint: Adjust the container name if yours differs.
existing.permsTitle: Let the agent write + reload the proxy
existing.permsIntro: Least-privilege grants for the config dir and the test/reload commands. <agent-user> and group nurproxy are placeholders.
existing.permsHostNote: The exact commands for THIS host (with the detected user) are also printed when you run apply.
existing.permsWiki: See the "Existing-mode permissions" wiki page for the full permission model and threat-model note.
existing.statusWaiting: Waiting for confirmation on the host…

servers.noneYetBody: Register the first backend an agent should forward traffic to — e.g. a web app on your LAN.
servers.onAgentNone: No servers on this agent yet.
servers.suggestedTitle: Suggested from this agent's nginx config
servers.suggestedNote: Discovered in nginx config; referenced by {{names}}
servers.addModalSub: A backend address one of your agents forwards traffic to.
servers.agentHint: The agent that will reach this server.

servers.removeConfirm: Remove this server? Domains pointing at it will be affected until you repoint them.

domains.title: Domains
domains.subtitle: Subdomains proxied to your servers.
domains.acmeWarningTitle: No HTTPS certificates are being issued
domains.acmeWarningBody: One or more domains use automatic TLS, but no Let's Encrypt contact email is configured — so no certificates can be issued and these domains stay on plaintext HTTP.
domains.noneYetBody: Create your first domain to start proxying traffic to a server.
domains.noMatchesBody: No domains match the current filters.
domains.subdomainApexHint: Tip: use @ for the zone root (apex).
domains.certOnlyHelp: NurProxy issues and renews the TLS certificate and installs it on the agent, but serves no vhost — you write the proxy config yourself and point it at the cert path. No public DNS record is managed.
domains.tlsWildcardHint: Serve this domain from one shared *.{{zone}} certificate instead of its own. Only for a single label directly below the zone; an imported certificate for this host still takes precedence.
domains.tlsWildcardUnavailable: Only a single label directly below the zone with central TLS can use the zone wildcard certificate.
domains.tlsWildcardWarning: The same private key is installed on every agent serving any wildcard domain of this zone. A compromise of one agent exposes the key for all of them. Prefer per-host certificates unless you need a wildcard.
domains.proxiedHint: Keep leaves an existing record as it is. A new record starts as DNS only.
domains.proxiedHelp: Cloudflare terminates public TLS for a proxied domain. NurProxy still serves the origin and keeps the origin certificate valid, so set the zone's SSL/TLS mode to Full (strict).
domains.dnsManaged: DNS: managed by NurProxy (deleted with the domain)
domains.dnsAdopted: DNS: existing record in use, not owned by NurProxy
domains.takeoverAdopt: {{fqdn}} already points at {{target}}. Nothing is deleted; NurProxy takes ownership of the record.
domains.takeoverCreate: {{fqdn}} has no record. Nothing is deleted; NurProxy creates the CNAME to {{target}}.
domains.takeoverOwnership: Afterwards NurProxy owns the CNAME to {{target}} and deletes it when the domain is deleted.
domains.accessLogHint: Off keeps visitor IPs of this domain out of the proxy's access log.
domains.errorLogLevelHint: crit keeps routine upstream errors (with client IPs) out of the error log.
domains.logUnsupported: The {{backend}} backend on this agent can't do this per domain, so saving a value other than the host default is refused.
domains.capUnsupported: The {{backend}} backend on this agent does not support this option — it will be ignored.
domains.manualConfigBody: Editing the raw config overrides the automatic config for this domain. Reset to automatic anytime.
domains.manualActiveBody: This domain no longer follows the generated config — it serves the manual override below.
domains.configBackend: Rendered for the serving agent's backend: {{backend}}
domains.bulkMsg_one: Delete {{count}} domain? Its DNS record and proxy config will be removed.
domains.bulkMsg_other: Delete {{count}} domains? Their DNS records and proxy configs will be removed.

settings.title: Settings
settings.appearanceSub: Pick the interface that suits you. Switch light/dark from the toggle in the navigation.
settings.reconcilerSub: How often NurProxy syncs DNS records and proxy configs.
settings.tlsSub: NurProxy issues free HTTPS certificates for your domains via Let's Encrypt (DNS-01). Set a contact email to enable automatic issuance and renewal.
settings.tlsPrivacyTitle: This email is only for Let's Encrypt
settings.tlsPrivacyBody: It is sent to the certificate authority (Let's Encrypt) for expiry and account notices only. It is not used to create a NurProxy account, never sent to the NurProxy maintainers, and you will not receive marketing from us.
settings.acmeEmailHelp: Until this is set, automatic HTTPS certificates are not issued. Changes take effect without a restart.
settings.adminApiKeySub: Use this as a <0>Bearer</0> token for programmatic access and the MCP server.
settings.copyNow: Copy this now — it won’t be shown again
settings.tokenHint: Needs <0>Zone → Read</0> and <1>DNS → Edit</1>. Stored encrypted at rest.
settings.providerCallout: Create a token in <0>Cloudflare → API Tokens</0> using the “Edit zone DNS” template. <1>Walkthrough →</1>
settings.tokenNoZones: Token is valid, but no zones were found. Check Zone → Read permission.
settings.safeAutoRepairSub: Automatically repair only faults that are proven to affect NurProxy-owned resources and have a typed reversible action.
settings.safeAutoRepairHint: Enabled by default. Per-agent overrides can inherit, enable, or disable this setting.
settings.pwTooShort: New password must be at least 8 characters.
settings.deleteProviderMsg: Delete this provider? All zones and domains using it will lose DNS management.
settings.removeZoneMsg: Remove this zone? Domains using it will lose DNS management.
settings.acmeStagingHelp: Staging certificates are NOT browser-trusted, but issuance does not count against production rate limits. Turn off for real certificates.

config.title: Config
config.subtitle: The central versioned store of proxy config NurProxy manages on your hosts. Diff, roll back, and review on-disk drift before it overwrites your changes.
config.noneBody: Once an agent applies a domain or adopts an existing config, its versioned artifacts appear here.
config.searchPlaceholder: Filter by file, domain, server, backend…
config.select: Select an artifact to view its content, history, and drift.
config.driftedBody: The content on the host no longer matches the accepted state. Review the diff, then Accept the on-disk content as the new live version or Reject to restore the accepted state.
config.driftChecksumOnly: The host reported a different checksum but hasn't sent its on-disk content yet (it arrives on the next apply). Accept to take the host's current state, or Reject to restore the accepted version now.
config.bulkRowNote: Accepted state shown; the host reported a checksum mismatch.
config.bulkBannerBody: Several configs changed on-disk at once (for example after an OS package update). Review them together and accept or reject all.
config.bulkModalWarn: Accept all promotes every host's on-disk content to the live state. Reject all restores the accepted state to every host.
config.maskFailed: Failed to parse the structured view.
config.maskAdvisory: This config can't be fully represented as a form yet, so the structured view is read-only. The raw text is authoritative.
config.maskBackendRawOnly: The structured view isn't available for this backend yet. Edit the raw config.
config.saved: Saved. The change will be applied on the host.
config.editFlipsManual: Editing the raw config will mark this artifact as Manual — it can no longer be re-rendered from the model without resetting.
config.resetToModelConfirm: Re-render this artifact from its domain model and discard the manual edits?
config.resetDone: Reset to the model. The agent will re-render on the next apply.

discovery.sectionSub: Sources NurProxy asks for machines your agents could proxy to. Discovery only suggests servers; you pick which to import.
discovery.modalSub: NurProxy reads QEMU VMs and LXC containers through the Proxmox API with an API token. The orchestrator must reach the API.
discovery.urlHint: Any cluster node. Without a port, 8006 is used.
discovery.tokenSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
discovery.tokenSecretRequired: Enter the secret again: the URL, token ID or TLS settings changed.
discovery.permissionsHint: A read-only token is enough: give it the PVEAuditor role on / (Sys.Audit, VM.Audit). Reading guest-agent addresses also needs VM.Monitor on PVE 8 (VM.GuestAgent.Audit on PVE 9); without it VMs fall back to their cloud-init address.
discovery.fingerprintHint: SHA-256 fingerprint from the node's Certificates page. When set, only this certificate is accepted, which works with the default self-signed certificate.
discovery.caPemHint: PEM of a CA to trust in addition to the system roots, e.g. the cluster's pve-root-ca.pem.
discovery.insecureWarning: Without verification or a fingerprint, anyone on the path could read the token. Pin the fingerprint if you can.
discovery.syncIntervalHint: Periodic runs show new machines and flag imported servers whose machine is gone.
discovery.deleteMsg: Delete this source? Servers imported from it stay as ordinary servers.
discovery.importSub: Pick the machines this agent should proxy to. Check each address: it must be reachable from the agent. Imported servers stay editable.
discovery.noResult: No result yet. Run discovery to list the machines.
discovery.needAddress_one: {{count}} selected machine has no address. Enter one or deselect it.
discovery.needAddress_other: {{count}} selected machines have no address. Enter one or deselect them.
discovery.skipped_one: {{count}} machine was already imported and skipped.
discovery.skipped_other: {{count}} machines were already imported and skipped.
discovery.missingList: No longer reported by the source: {{names}}. The servers are kept; remove them if the machines are gone for good.
discovery.goneTitle: The discovery source has not reported this machine since {{when}}.
